message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc reported revenue of 1.85 billion dollars for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, up 36.54% on the year before and 7.51% on the previous quarter [D1]. Net income was 397 million dollars, up 107.85%, on a net margin of 21.51% and a gross margin of 65.87%, and earnings per share of 2.82 came in against an estimate of 2.16 [D1]. The Communications Solutions Group produced revenue of 1.35 billion dollars and operating income of 458 million dollars, up 86.18%, while the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group produced revenue of 501 million dollars and operating income of 155 million dollars, up 68.48% [D1]. Total segment operating income of 613 million dollars was up 81.36% [D1]. Guidance for the current quarter is revenue of 1.93 billion dollars to 1.95 billion dollars, growth of 37%, and earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 on a diluted share count of about 172 million [D1]. Total assets stood at 11.92 billion dollars, shareholders equity at 6.57 billion dollars and net debt at 141 million dollars [D1].

The argument in the market is about which constraint binds, and management gave both sides of it, saying demand is far exceeding its ability to supply, that the pipeline continues to grow strongly, that orders should be slightly up from the third quarter and that the 6G opportunity is larger than the 5G cycle [D3]. The counter-argument comes from the same call, where management said supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue, that the supply situation is likely to be nonlinear and that the one-time tariff impacts this year will not repeat [D3]. Bulls also lean on the mix shift in wireline, where manufacturing is taking a larger share of a business that was historically research and development led as AI data centre build-outs scale [D4]. Price action keeps the debate live, with the close of 333.42 above the 20-day average of 330.47 and the 50-day average of 326.21 in an uptrend, immediate support spanning 300.87 to 332.78 against immediate resistance at 366.41, and the largest five-session advance on file at 28.62% from 2026-02-17 against a largest five-session decline of 13.98% from 2026-08-17 [D2].

The plan is to hold into the print and let the guided range do the work, because revenue of 1.93 billion dollars to 1.95 billion dollars and earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 are the only figures management has put on the record for the current quarter [D1]. The confirming evidence would be revenue at or above 1.95 billion dollars and earnings per share at or above 3.40 [D1]. The disconfirming evidence would be revenue below 1.93 billion dollars or earnings per share below 3.34 [D1]. Margins are the second test, since a gross margin below 65.87% or a net margin below 21.51% would say the fiscal 2026 lift that management said will not repeat is already fading [D3].

Sizing should reflect that the shares already carry a forward price to earnings of 20.66 against a trailing price to earnings of 45.89, which is a valuation of the guide rather than of the reported quarter [D5]. No dated event beyond the current reporting cycle is on file, so the range itself is the catalyst [D1]. The plan therefore is to hold through the print, add only on evidence that supply is converting demand into revenue, and reduce if the guided range is missed on either line [D1].
